t:
(a) Consolidation.—Section 2663 of title 10, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following new subsection:“(h) Land Acquisition Options in Advance of Military Construction Projects.—(1) The Secretary of a military department may acquire an option on a parcel of real property before or after its acquisition is authorized by law, if the Secretary considers it suitable and likely to be needed for a military project of the military department under the jurisdiction of the Secretary.“(2) As consideration for an option acquired under paragraph (1), the Secretary may pay, from funds available to the military department under the jurisdiction of the Secretary for real property activities, an amount that is not more than 12 percent of the appraised fair market value of the property.”. 
    (b) Repeal of Superseded Provision.—
        (1) Repeal.—Section 2677 of such title is repealed. 
        (2) Clerical amendment.—The table of sections at the beginning of chapter 159 of such title is amended by striking the item relating to section 2677.

fable.w: The section lets a military department Secretary buy options on real property at the Secretary's own discretion and repeals a superseded provision. The tempting reading is that buying an option from a landowner involves an outside party, but that is a commercial transaction, not consultation, comment, a hearing, an advisory body, or a right to sue over a federal decision. No rulemaking or outside input is required before the Secretary acts.
fable.s: The Secretary of a military department may acquire an option on a parcel of real property before or after its acquisition is authorized by law

qwen_block.w: This section grants authority to a federal official (the Secretary of a military department) to acquire land options. The decision-making process described is internal to the federal government, relying on the Secretary's own judgment of suitability. There is no requirement to consult with, coordinate with, or obtain input from any outside parties such as the public, state governments, or private entities before making this decision.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary of a military department may acquire an option on a parcel of real property before or after its acquisition is authorized by law, if the Secretary considers it suitable and likely to be needed for a military project of the military department under the jurisdiction of the Secretary.

opus.w: This section lets the Secretary buy options on real property and sets a cap on what can be paid for them. The Secretary decides on his own judgment, without consulting, holding hearings with, or hearing objections from anyone outside the federal government. The seller of the option is involved only as a counterparty to a contract, and the definition excludes contracts. So the private landowner does not make this participation.
opus.s: The Secretary of a military department may acquire an option on a parcel of real property before or after its acquisition is authorized by law, if the Secretary considers it suitable and likely to be needed for a military project
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The Secretary acquires an option from a private landowner and pays for it based on an appraised value, so an outside party is involved. This fails because buying property, or an option on it, is a contract transaction. The landowner is a counterparty to a deal, not someone consulted before a federal decision. The definition excludes contracts. Nothing in the section creates a comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation duty or right to sue. Subsection (b) is only a repeal and a clerical amendment.

qwen_chat.w: This section grants the Secretary of a military department the authority to acquire land options based on their own determination of suitability. It does not require consultation, coordination, or input from any outside parties such as states, tribes, the public, or experts. The decision rests entirely within the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary of a military department may acquire an option on a parcel of real property before or after its acquisition is authorized by law, if the Secretary considers it suitable and likely to be needed for a military project of the military department under the jurisdiction of the Secretary.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the Secretary must consult with property owners or local governments to acquire an option, implying participation. However, the text only grants the Secretary the authority to acquire options based on their own judgment ("if the Secretary considers it suitable"). It does not mandate any consultation, hearing, or coordination with outside parties. The interaction with a property owner to buy an option is a contractual transaction, not a participatory decision-making process as defined.
